name: Torres del Paine W Trek
summary: A four- or five-day walk along the south side of the Paine massif, taking in the Torres base viewpoint, the French Valley and Grey Glacier. Nights are in refugios or serviced campsites, all of which must be booked before entry.

name: Torres del Paine O Circuit
summary: The full loop around the Cordillera del Paine, about 110–120 km, adding the quiet northern back side to the W. Its high point is Paso John Gardner above Grey Glacier, and the back section is walked in one direction only and opens when CONAF says so.

name: Torres del Paine Q Circuit
summary: The O Circuit with the approach leg from the park administration up to Paine Grande added at the start, roughly 17 km and a day more. Same high point at Paso John Gardner, same booking and one-way rules on the back side.

name: Dientes de Navarino Trek
summary: A loop of roughly 40–50 km from Puerto Williams on Isla Navarino, through peat bog, scree and beech forest below the Dientes ridge. There is no maintained trail and no shelter on the route, so navigation and self-sufficiency matter more than the modest daily distances suggest.

name: Huemul Circuit Trek
summary: A four-day loop of about 60 km from El Chaltén over Paso del Viento and Paso Huemul, with long views over the Southern Patagonian Ice Field and Viedma Glacier. Two river crossings are made by Tyrolean traverse, and the park rangers check harness, pulley and other gear before they will register the walk.

name: O'Higgins Glacier Trek
summary: A remote out-and-back from Candelario Mancilla, reached by boat across Lago O'Higgins, toward the face of Glaciar O'Higgins on the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. The path is faint and poorly marked, and the boat that starts and ends the trip is regularly cancelled by wind.

name: Cerro Castillo Circuit
summary: Despite the name this is a point-to-point traverse of about 53 km through Cerro Castillo National Park, from Las Horquetas on the Carretera Austral to Villa Cerro Castillo. The high point is Paso El Peñón, reached by a long climb over loose scree and often crossed in strong wind.

name: Cochamo Valley Trek
summary: A muddy four- to five-hour walk in from El Morro to the camps at La Junta, used as a base for day walks up to the granite walls, waterfalls and viewpoints above the valley. Camping is capacity-limited and must be reserved in advance in high season.

name: Villa O'Higgins–El Chalten Trek
summary: The walking border crossing between the end of the Carretera Austral and El Chaltén: a boat across Lago O'Higgins to Candelario Mancilla, about 22 km on foot over the Paso Dos Lagunas frontier to Lago del Desierto, then a second boat and a road transfer. It can be done in a day, but most take two, and both boats are weather-dependent.

name: Fitz Roy / El Chalten Trek
summary: The standard multi-day link-up of El Chaltén's two main valleys, camping at De Agostini below Cerro Torre and at Poincenot below Fitz Roy. The high point is Laguna de los Tres, reached by a steep final climb of around 400 m from the campsite.

name: Laguna de los Tres Trek
summary: A 20–25 km there-and-back day walk from El Chaltén up the Río Blanco valley to the lake below Fitz Roy, usually 8 to 9 hours. Easy going until the last hour, which climbs roughly 400 m of steep, rough ground to the lip of the moraine.

name: Patagonia O'Higgins Trek
summary: A loose commercial name for trekking out of Villa O'Higgins at the southern end of the Carretera Austral rather than one fixed route; operators use it for the Glaciar O'Higgins walk, for the border crossing to El Chaltén, or for a combination of the two. Because it is not a single published route, no duration, difficulty, high point or season can be stated for it here.
